title: bug: daemon checkPortablePath DEVICE_NAME accepts 'CON .txt' (device name + spaces + extension)
description: packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/workloadSnapshot.ts DEVICE_NAME `/^(?:con|…)(?:\..*)?$/i` accepts 'CON .txt' / 'COM1 .log', which Git's is_valid_win32_path treats as reserved (spaces before '.' are skipped). Fix: add ' *' before the optional extension, as scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs does since CQ-R09a. Low risk: Windows 11 creates such names as plain files; this is conservative-portability parity only.
definitionOfDone: checkPortablePath refuses 'CON .txt', 'a/aux  .c' and 'COM1 .log' while still accepting 'con x' and 'console.log', proven by test rows in the workloadSnapshot tests

implementationPlan.note: Added 3 BAD_PATHS rows (CON .txt, a/aux  .c with two spaces, COM1 .log) and the 'accepts names that only begin with a device name' test. Red proof in isolated snapshot /tmp (whole-repo git archive HEAD + this test file, native node_modules symlink, env -i): 3 failed, 152 passed (the three new rows only; acceptance test passes). Shared checkout has many peer dirty paths, untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Make the daemon rule identical to the local-runner gate, and make the comments in both files say so. These are regex and comment edits only, in LF and pure ASCII.

(a) packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/workloadSnapshot.ts:116. Replace the DEVICE_NAME line with a byte-for-byte copy of scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs line 40. The copy adds ' *' before the optional extension. It also spells the superscripts as ¹²³ escapes, which are the same code points with the same semantics, and leaves the daemon module pure ASCII. Put this comment line directly above it:
// Like Git's is_valid_win32_path, spaces before the extension are skipped: 'CON .txt' is reserved too.

Error handling: unchanged by design, and nothing new to add.
- A newly refused segment takes the existing branch in checkPortablePath: invalidInput(field, `${shown} uses a Windows device name`).
- That is the same INVALID_INPUT code and field the callers already handle. `shown` is the quoted, printable-ASCII form of the path, so no raw input reaches an error message or log.
- Add no new error code, message or try/catch.

(b) scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs, comments only. Do not touch line 40 or any other line.
- Line 5: change '...: FORBIDDEN_CHAR, wellFormed and foldCase verbatim, DEVICE_NAME widened. Facts relied on:' to '...: FORBIDDEN_CHAR, DEVICE_NAME, wellFormed and foldCase verbatim. Facts relied on:'.
- Line 39: replace "// The daemon's rule plus ' *': like Git's is_valid_win32_path, 'CON .txt' is reserved too." with the same comment line as in (a).
Its S10 test scans this source file. Keep the file ASCII, and never write import(, require(, process., node:fs, child_process or a `from '...'` phrase, even in a comment.

Read-only checks in the shared tree:
- `diff <(sed -n 40p scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs) <(grep '^const DEVICE_NAME' packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/workloadSnapshot.ts)` prints nothing.
- The same holds for the comment lines: `sed -n 39p` against `grep -B1 '^const DEVICE_NAME' ... | head -1`.
- `LC_ALL=C grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7f]'` finds nothing in either file.
- `git diff --numstat` over the three task files shows about +12/-3. The prototype measured ts 2/1, test 8/0 and mjs 2/2.
implementationPlan.note: DEVICE_NAME line in workloadSnapshot.ts is now byte-identical to source-snapshot.mjs:40 (diff empty, ¹²³ as \u escapes, both files pure ASCII, LF); comment line identical in both; mjs lines 5 and 39 comment-only edits. numstat ts 2/1, test 8/0, mjs 2/2. No new error paths: refusals reuse invalidInput(field, '<quoted path> uses a Windows device name').

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of this task's diff. Load adversarial-self-review first.

Mutation probes run only in a scratch copy of the step-3 snapshot, against src/benchmarks/workloadSnapshot.test.ts:
(1) Drop ' *' from the daemon regex. The three new rows must fail.
(2) Over-widen it to `(?:[ .].*)?$`. The acceptance test must fail on 'con x'.
(3) Make it prefix-only, `/^(?:con|...|lpt[...])/i`. The acceptance test must fail on 'console.log'.
(4) Change the ¹ escape to ´. The existing 'superscript COM device' row must fail. The byte-identical diff from step 2 guards ² and ³.

Also check:
- The semantics match Git's is_valid_win32_path. A device name followed by any spaces and then '.', ':' or the end of the segment is reserved. Anything else ('con x', 'console.log', 'com10') is not. FORBIDDEN_CHAR already refuses ':', and the segment rule already refuses a trailing space, so the regex needs no ':' branch.
- Error handling: each new refusal surfaces as the existing INVALID_INPUT with the quoted path. Nothing throws a different error type or echoes raw input.
- The change only refuses more. No workload digest changes, and step 3's benchmark run shows that no corpus fixture is now refused.
- grep confirms that nothing outside packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks imports workloadSnapshot.
- Only the three task files changed. Peers' dirty paths were not touched.

If anything changed, rerun the step-3 command fresh before complete_task.

Semantics match is_valid_win32_path (name + spaces + '.'/end); ':' already refused by FORBIDDEN_CHAR. Refusals reuse existing INVALID_INPUT with quoted path; the change only refuses more, and no corpus fixture is refused (benchmarks 304 passed). planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(a) Insert only ' *' and leave the literal superscripts and source-snapshot.mjs as they are. Rejected because source-snapshot.mjs would then describe a divergence that no longer exists: its header says 'DEVICE_NAME widened' and line 39 says "The daemon's rule plus ' *'". That file is a security gate, and QA already enforced the accuracy of its comments in R09a. With a byte-identical line, 'verbatim' is true and parity can be checked with a one-line diff.
(b) Share one rule between the two modules. Rejected: source-snapshot.mjs must stay dependency-free pure ESM (S10 allows only node:crypto), and the daemon module is TypeScript.
(c) A cross-package test that asserts the two lines match. Rejected: it would couple the daemon's tests to scripts/.
(d) The full daemon npm test. Not needed: the module is test-only, and every importer is in src/benchmarks.
The architect prototype in a scratch snapshot measured +12/-3 over 3 files.
- RED at HEAD 981784e: 3 failed, 152 passed.
- GREEN: benchmarks 7 files, 304 passed + 6 skipped (HEAD 300 + 6). local-runner-snapshot 14/14.
- Package tsc and test-file tsc both exited 0.
- Over-widened and prefix-only mutants were both killed by the acceptance test.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- checkPortablePath (workloadSnapshot.ts:188) tests DEVICE_NAME against foldCase(segment) for every '/'-segment. It guards the file-map keys (initialFiles, assessmentFiles, digestFiles) and source.paths.
- On a refusal it throws invalidInput(field, '<quoted path> uses a Windows device name'), so error handling is already in place. The BAD_PATHS it.each asserts INVALID_INPUT in all four placements. referenceDigest in the test file is an independent digest oracle.
- FORBIDDEN_CHAR already refuses ':', and the segment rule refuses leading or trailing spaces and a trailing dot. So ' *' is the only gap against Git's is_valid_win32_path.
- Both files are LF. After the change, both are pure ASCII.
- isEpicFinal:true comes from the old highest-order rule. The epic's real final task is CQ-R13.
planningNotes.risks:
- The shared node_modules is Windows-native. Run vitest only in an isolated snapshot of the WHOLE repo: a partial archive fails non-routineWorkloads.test.ts with ENOENT (seen while prototyping).
- S10 in local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs scans source-snapshot.mjs. A non-ASCII character or a banned substring (import(, require(, process., node:fs, child_process, from '...') in a comment fails it.
- 'a/aux  .c' has two spaces. Copy the ¹²³ escapes exactly: only the step-2 diff guards ² and ³.
- QA may read isEpicFinal:true as needing a full-epic gate. Step 3 explains why it does not.
- The checkout is shared: report only the three files and never touch peers' dirty paths.
